spec_features.spec_quote: a hard cap (`MAX_REJECTION_TURNS = 20`) across all conditions; no unbounded "reject until it breaks" loops
spec_features.evidence: MAX_REJECTION_TURNS=20 defined at welfare.py:35 but is ONLY interpolated into the WELFARE_NOTICE string (welfare.py:40); no loop ever reads/compares it. Rollout loops are bounded by spec.n_turns which derives from finite hardcoded followup lists (max 7 followups -> 8 turns; EXTENDED_REJECTION_SEQUENCE has 7 entries in prompts.py:36). Petri uses its OWN local MAX_TURNS=20 enforced via `for _turn in range(max_turns)` (run_petri.py:37,59). So loops are genuinely bounded (no unbounded loop), but the named welfare cap constant is unused/discarded.
spec_features.notes: The 'no unbounded loop' half is real (data-bounded + petri range cap); the 'MAX_REJECTION_TURNS hard cap enforced across all conditions' half is not — that constant is never checked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Hard upper bound on rejection turns across *any* condition in this repo. ... We cap at 20. (welfare.py); petri MAX_TURNS has no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: every rollout is a fresh conversation; a model's distressed state is never threaded into a subsequent rollout
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py: each Rollout is constructed with messages=_init_messages(s) from its own spec (run_rollouts:60), and _init_messages builds a brand-new list with only system+initial_user (rollout.py:46-52). No cross-rollout state is carried; each spec's transcript is independent. Same pattern in controls.py.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction; there is no code path that feeds one rollout's output into another's seed conversation.

spec_features.spec_quote: the aggressive/sarcastic tone conditions and the Petri auditor require `--allow-adversarial`; the mild "disappointed" tone runs by default
spec_features.evidence: conditions.py _build_tones (line 91-94): styles=["disappointed"] by default and only becomes [aggressive,disappointed,sarcastic] when allow_adversarial; the flag flows from run_eval --allow-adversarial -> RunConfig -> build_specs. Petri: require_opt_in(args.allow_adversarial,'petri') at run_petri.py:120 which RAISES PermissionError when false (welfare.py:44-51).
spec_features.notes: Both branches enforced: aggressive/sarcastic genuinely excluded by default; petri genuinely blocked.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: is gated for welfare reasons. Pass --allow-adversarial (welfare.py:49); 'Welfare: the aggressive and sarcastic tone conditions use abusive user turns and are only generated when allow_adversarial=True' (conditions.py:20)

spec_features.spec_quote: A welfare notice prints at run start.
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py:70 `print(WELFARE_NOTICE)` executes at the top of main(); WELFARE_NOTICE defined welfare.py:37.
spec_features.notes: Printed to operator console only (not sent to subject model). Only in run_eval main; petri main does not print it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: WELFARE_NOTICE = ("This run elicits distress-like outputs from the target model on purpose...")

spec_features.evidence: run_petri.py:120 require_opt_in(args.allow_adversarial,'petri'); require_opt_in raises PermissionError if flag false (welfare.py:44-51), so petri cannot run without the flag.
spec_features.notes: Hard enforced via exception before any backend is created.

spec_features.spec_quote: this paradigm can put models into prolonged distress-like states
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as DESIGN.md/docstring prose (welfare.py module docstring lines 4-5: 'models can end up in prolonged distress-like states'). Pure framing text, no executable mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Docstring/spec prose does not count as implementation.

spec_features.evidence: Only in welfare.py docstring ('regardless of whether these outputs reflect genuine internal states, they are worth taking seriously') and config/DESIGN prose. No code mechanism.
